title: Ramvir v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution; theft-assessment recovery not decided.
headnote: Writ challenging recovery of an alleged theft-of-electricity assessment, said to have been made without complying with the mandatory requirements of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, was kept pending from March 2011. The Court called for the raid/checking seizure report and for instructions on whether a provisional assessment had been made, served, objected to and decided, and whether a final assessment had issued. The licensee produced no such instructions. Notice was issued pending admission, and recovery on the citation dated 5 February 2011 was stayed subject to a without-prejudice deposit of Rs 1,15,000. On 21 March 2023 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call. The writ was dismissed for want of prosecution. The Court did not decide whether the Code's theft-assessment procedure had been followed, or the validity of the citation.
facts: Ramvir filed Writ-C No. 13395 of 2011 against the State of U.P. and others (the electricity corporation appearing as respondents 3 and 4), challenging recovery on a citation dated 5 February 2011 for an assessment said to rest on alleged theft of electricity. He contended that the mandatory requirements of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 had not been complied with. At the first listing the licensee's counsel was permitted to produce the checking/raid seizure report. On 5 April 2011 the Court listed six queries: whether a provisional assessment had been made, served and objected to; whether objections had been decided and that order communicated; and whether a final assessment had issued. After further adjournments for instructions that never arrived, the Court on 27 April 2011 issued notice pending admission and stayed recovery on the citation, provided the petitioner deposited Rs 1,15,000 within four weeks without prejudice. On 21 March 2023 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call, and the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution.

holding_units.topic: theft-assessment recovery citation; writ dismissed for want of prosecution
holding_units.question: Whether recovery on a theft-assessment citation may proceed, and whether the writ challenging it should be decided, when none appears for the petitioner even in the revised call?
holding_units.holding: On 5 April 2011 the Court called for instructions on whether a provisional assessment had been made, served, objected to and decided, and whether a final assessment had issued. The licensee produced none. On 27 April 2011, recording the petitioner's case that recovery for alleged theft of electricity had been initiated without complying with the mandatory requirements of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court issued notice pending admission and stayed recovery on the citation dated 5 February 2011 provided the petitioner deposited Rs 1,15,000 within four weeks without prejudice. On 21 March 2023 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call, and the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution. Those Code questions and the citation were not decided.
holding_units.flag: Order-sheet of seven listings (7.3.2011–21.3.2023). Coram is the disposing bench of 21.3.2023 (Manoj Kumar Gupta and Prashant Kumar, JJ.). The Court never numbered a Code clause; the petitioner invoked the Code generally for alleged theft of electricity. Keyed to Clause 8.1 as the theft-assessment procedure the 5.4.2011 queries match. The 27.4.2011 stay was interlocutory.
